newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to ban German beef imports over BSE fears.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to ban German beef imports over BSE fears.

text.p: Ukraine will ban imports of German beef starting this week to prevent the risk of contamination from bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), known as mad cow disease, Health Minister Andriy Serdyuk said on Monday.
"We have accepted the decision to ban imports of beef from Germany to prevent the threat of introducing mad cow disease on our territory," Serdyuk told Reuters.

Ukraine imports only small amounts of beef from Germany, which initially reported a local case of mad cow disease in January. Bonn officials have since said that the infected calf had been imported from Britain and that Germany was BSE free.
"Luckily this disease has not been found in Ukraine," Serdyuk said.
Ukraine imported live cattle worth $65,000 and exported $2 million in January. Meat exports stood at $22 million, mainly to Russia and eastern Europe, and imports totalled $15 million.
